raw_new_expert_decision.quote:
Cividini-

Motta and Ahearn (2013) utilized the MSA to

determine relative reinforcer ef ﬁ cacy within the

context of differential reinforcement contingen-

cies to reduce prompt dependency. For three of

the four learners included in the study, the com-
bination of tokens plus praise was more rein-

forcing than either in isolation.

Together, the results of these two studies

demonstrate that the MSA can be an effective

and ef ﬁ cient way to determine the reinforcing

value of stimuli, including tokens. The current

research sought to systematically replicate

Smaby et al. (2007) and Cividini-Motta and

Ahearn’s (2013) use of the MSA, speci ﬁ cally to

evaluate the relative reinforcing ef ﬁ cacy of the

individual components of a token economy in
a brief assessment.
raw_new_expert_decision.reason: Although the authors state that they sought to 'systematically replicate Smaby et al. (2007) and Cividini-Motta and Ahearn’s (2013) use of the MSA', the full text establishes that Cividini-Motta and Ahearn (2013; 10.1002/jaba.67, 'Effects of two variations of differential reinforcement on prompt dependency') supplied the assessment procedure, star-pointing task (Method, p. 3, lines 477-489), and fixed component order (Design, p. 4, lines 655-663) rather than a retested empirical finding. Cividini-Motta and Ahearn (2013) tested differential reinforcement variations (tokens plus praise vs. either alone) to reduce prompt dependency, whereas Fiske et al. (2019) evaluate token-economy components (token without backup, yoked FR, token with backup, primary reinforcement) and compare those substantive findings to Fiske et al. (2015) in the Discussion (pp. 5-6, lines 886-926). Under the codebook, reusing an assessment method, task, or design from an earlier study without retesting its empirical finding is not an omitted replication target.
